🎥 "Sorna's Catastrophe": The Fallout from Closing an Autism Center

The death of Sorna, a 20-year-old autistic young man, has been a bitter and devastating loss for his family, friends, acquaintances, and the autism spectrum community.

Most participants in the roundtable of autism families cite the closure of a center where he spent hours as one of the most important causes of Sorna's catastrophe.

A center for the care and education of autistic children in central Tehran has been shut down, and no replacement has been introduced.

Most families on the autism spectrum describe the existence of such centers as essential and a lifeline for themselves, and they strongly reproach those responsible for closing that center.

A suggestion for teachers and educators of children and adolescents: One of the most important skills and lessons that should be introduced in our educational system is rhetoric, oratory—or what we might call the art of presentation. Our children should be able to present any speech, data, or content in a completely eloquent, fluent, straightforward, engaging, and concise manner. The essay-writing class in our time was perhaps a minimal exercise in this very area, but it carried no weight and was treated as a recreational sideshow! Today, presentation skills are a key skill worldwide, and many institutions and companies have their own brand ambassadors or specialized presenters. Now that this skill is not part of the educational curriculum, we ourselves can practice these things and, alongside conversations and class materials, carry out exercises practically and jointly with ourselves and our students. The largest and most difficult meetings in our country typically fail to reach a conclusion precisely because of this problem and lack of capability. That is not the whole problem, but it is a significant part of it.

Watch this video. Sometimes, because we don't see something with our own eyes, we assume it's a minor issue or doesn't exist at all. From morning to night, how many people with disabilities do you see on the street? Do you see only a few? The reason isn't that their numbers are small; many of them stay at home, because society hasn't made it possible for them to be present. The same is true of autism. When you look at the statistics, you realize what an ocean of problems we're facing. Today, roughly one in every 127 births is a person born with autism spectrum disorder. There's no screening or prior detection either. That means if we have one million births a year in Iran, nearly 8,000 people are added to the population of people with autism every year. Now watch this video. Officials in Tehran had concluded that a "City of Autism" should be created; a place to provide various services to children and people with autism. The issue is so big that they've talked about it on IRIB and defined a project of this scale for it.♨️But the project, amid the mismatches, conflicts, record-building, and obstacles that managers put in each other's way, apparently has now come to a halt. My point is this: what we don't see isn't necessarily small. Sometimes it's just been removed from public life to such an extent that it doesn't catch my eye or yours.@yaser_arab57

A few days ago, the President's Office called to follow up on the autism issue. Of course, I had no expectation. I had also told friends and families that I was only seeking a people-driven solution to the problem within our own capabilities. Anyway, today a meeting was held at the Deputy for Public Communications of the President's Office, and I and several other dear ones participated.
1. Truly, the conditions inside the government and the issue of persons with disabilities and the situation of experts are very intertwined, lacking precise understanding, necessary executive backing, destructive parallel work, etc., such that I doubt the autism issue will be solved in a process-oriented and problem-based manner in the country anytime soon.
2. Ultimately, a National Autism Organization must be created, which neither the government will accept nor the Planning and Budget Organization. The President does not want to enlarge the government (he lacks the power to shrink it where it should be shrunk), and the head of the Planning and Budget Organization does not want a new budget line to open.
3. It was agreed that for now, four to five main priorities agreed upon by parents, practitioners, and trainers would be agreed upon, and next month, in a meeting, all relevant officials would be invited, and there the fate of these four or five specific issues would at least be clarified.
P.S.: One of the miseries of our country is the lack of wisdom in the workforce. So-and-so from such-and-such organization has gotten into a spat with so-and-so from such-and-such association! For a long time, such-and-such matter that should have been resolved has been left silent and suspended!

That's just how it is... This is the job!
Correction;
I mean, these are the coordinates of work and working in the country, that's just how it is... It is not a standard situation, and one must work under these same conditions... If we ourselves want to work independently, in a hundred places we will be forced to interact with this same structure... @yaser_arab57

entry.title: [yaser_arab57] Work? Get it to the Social and Cultural Deputy of Tehran Municipality. Hello…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @yaser_arab57

Work? Get it to the Social and Cultural Deputy of Tehran Municipality. Hello and without preamble! We are facing a serious issue in the country called autism and other intellectual and developmental disabilities. An issue that has no single, clear authority and is scattered among various bodies, from education and welfare to other institutions. The result of this scattering, for many families, is nothing but placelessness and lack of planning for their children; children who have no place to be present, play, communicate, and participate socially. In the meantime, neighborhood houses can be one of the closest and most accessible urban capacities for these families. However, families have gone to neighborhood houses, given their numbers, heard promises of a call, and then heard nothing. Sometimes the neighborhood house says: "Autism is specialized and not our job." The answer is that the neighborhood house is not supposed to be a therapist. It is enough for it to be an accessible public space for the neighborhood's families. Sometimes it says: "This issue is not defined in our program." The answer is: isn't the neighborhood house meant to deal with the real problems of the neighborhood's people? Sometimes it says: "Autism is the job of the Welfare Organization." The answer is that an autistic child, before being a file of any institution, is a member of this very neighborhood. And when this close and accessible door is also closed to the family, the result is not just an unanswered call; the family returns to the same wandering and loneliness as before, and the child loses another possibility of being in society. Hasn't the time come for the Social and Cultural Deputy of Tehran Municipality to take the role of neighborhood houses seriously in dealing with this issue? @yaser_arab57

entry.title: [yaser_arab57] From a bad school to a good school! ✍ Yaser Arab ✅ We all know that…
entry.summary:
Machine-translated from the original Telegram post.

Source: @yaser_arab57

From a bad school to a good school!
✍ Yaser Arab
✅ We all know that teachers' livelihoods are not good. The gap between many teachers' salaries and real living costs and the poverty line is serious and worrying.
✅ The protests, campaigns, and demands being made by teachers these days are understandable, and the demand for a dignified life is undoubtedly their indisputable right.
✅ But the issue of education is not just teachers' livelihoods. Even if all teachers' salaries were increased tomorrow, big questions about schools and education in Iran would still remain.
✅ What should be done with the content of textbooks? What exactly should our children learn, and what do they not learn? What new training and skills do teachers need to face today's world? How is the school managed, and to what extent does our school management structure align with the needs of today's child, family, and society? What is the student's share in school? What is the family's share? And what world is the school supposed to prepare the student for? What is the idea on the ground, and what is the possibility of movement under the current conditions of blockage?
✅ These are issues whose answers cannot be found solely in the government's annual budget. The government may have more or less money. Teachers' salaries may increase or not. But many fundamental issues of education will remain in place. The quality of education, educational content, teacher training and empowerment, school structure, and the relationship between school and children's real lives are issues we must think about independently of the perennial fight over the budget.
✅ This Thursday, September 10 (19 Shahrivar), alongside the demand for "a better livelihood for teachers," we will raise another question more seriously: How can we go from a bad school to a good school?
✅ For this reason, we have decided to hold a meeting with the presence of teachers and those concerned about education; a meeting to listen!
✅ We want to sit together, see the issues more precisely, hear experiences, and think about ways that might improve the state of education in Iran by one step.
✅ We invite all teachers, researchers, education activists, school principals, students, and all those concerned about education to participate in this conversation.
Time: Thursday, 19 Shahrivar 1405 (September 10, 2026), at 4:30 PM
Location: Palestine Street, Italia Street, No. 36, Ensaaf News Base. We look forward to seeing you.
☘@yaser_arab57
